questions.prompt: What is Constellation's core job for the club?
questions.explanation: Constellation holds the state of the work. Chat is built to move forward; it cannot tell you the state of anything. Constellation does not replace Slack — it tells Slack when something needs you.

answers.text: To hold the current state of the club's work somewhere that doesn't scroll away
To replace Slack as the place the club talks
To store the club's CAD files and documents

questions.prompt: You want to know whether the hydroponics wiring is finished. Where is the authoritative answer?
questions.explanation: The column a task sits in is the truth about its state — not what someone said in chat and not what anyone remembers agreeing to. That is the entire premise of the board.

answers.text: The column its task sits in on the project board
The most recent message in the project's Slack channel
Whoever you last spoke to about it

questions.prompt: Constellation is meant to replace Slack for club conversation.
questions.explanation: False. Slack stays the place you talk. What changes is that Constellation notifies you there when something actually needs you, so you do not have to remember to check a project tool.

questions.prompt: Why does Constellation award XP, ranks, and doubloons?
questions.explanation: Club work is volunteer work, and volunteer work nobody notices is work that stops happening. The reward system is the product noticing — it is not there to pressure anyone into working more hours.

answers.text: Because volunteer work that nobody notices tends to stop happening
To rank members against each other for officer selection
To pressure members into logging more hours
Because the software was built on a game engine
